playground.label: A small picture made with Pillow: pixels, the (left, top) origin, colour names and a flip (nothing is read from or written to a file)
playground.code:
from PIL import Image, ImageColor
size = input('Size of the picture in pixels, width x height (try 4x3): ')
w, h = (int(n) for n in size.lower().split('x'))
im = Image.new('RGBA', (w, h), 'white')
for x in range(w):
    for y in range(h):
        im.putpixel((x, y), (x * 255 // max(w - 1, 1), y * 255 // max(h - 1, 1), 128, 255))
print(im.size, im.mode)
print('top-left    ', im.getpixel((0, 0)))
print('bottom-right', im.getpixel((w - 1, h - 1)))
print('crop box (1, 1, 3, 2) size:', im.crop((1, 1, 3, 2)).size, '(right and bottom edges are left out)')
print(ImageColor.getcolor('CornflowerBlue', 'RGBA'))
flip = im.transpose(Image.Transpose.FLIP_LEFT_RIGHT)
print('after the flip, the old top-left is at the top-right:', flip.getpixel((w - 1, 0)) == im.getpixel((0, 0)))

findings: Appendix B

Appendix B answers question 6 with im.crop((0, 50, 50, 50)), whose size is (50, 0), where (0, 50, 50, 100) gives the 50 by 50 lower-left quarter; it calls the box left, top, width and height in answer 3 where the chapter says right and bottom; and it states in answer 12 that plt.show() resets the graph data [P01] [P06].
Background

Chapter 21 of the 3rd edition, Making Graphs and Manipulating Images, teaches Pillow and Matplotlib: colours as RGBA tuples and box tuples, the Image methods crop, copy, paste, resize, rotate and transpose with getpixel and putpixel, Project 16 Add a Logo, drawing with ImageDraw and text with ImageFont, the clipboard through pyperclipimg, and line, scatter, bar and pie graphs; it ends with 12 practice questions and 3 practice programs, Tile Maker, the photo folder finder and the seating cards [P01]. The page was fetched on 2026-10-13 and returned 200 with 119,144 bytes, holds 31 listings, 20 figures and 1 table, and its sha256 equals the chapterDigest the book's own chapter ontology records [P01] [P03] [P04].
Eleven interpreters

One program of 35 items (Pillow colours, crop, paste, resize, rotate, flip, pixels, drawing, fonts and Matplotlib figures, pie and bar) printed the same under 11 interpreters, Python 3.11.17, 3.12.3, 3.13.14, 3.14.0 to 3.14.6 and 3.15.0b4, each with Pillow 12.3.0 and Matplotlib 3.11.2; every difference found came from the releases of the packages, not of Python [P39] [P40] [P60].
Not executed

Nothing ran on Windows or macOS, so the Windows fill and the paths of listing 4 are read, not run; the PDFs of the JPEG standard and of JFIF were reached but their text was not searched; the repository commit the course pins was not opened; and the photograph of the stories was not fetched because the single request to Wikimedia Commons answered 429 [P44] [P45] [P01].
Pillow releases

Across 14 Pillow releases from 9.5.0 to 12.3.0, ImageDraw.textsize and ImageFont.getsize existed only in 9.5.0 and were removed in 10.0.0; the default font became a FreeType font, Aileron Regular, in 10.1.0 and load_default(size=) was accepted from then on; Image.filename was an absolute path in 10.3.0, 10.4.0 and 11.0.0 and the plain name in the others; and Image.getdata() gives a DeprecationWarning from 12.1.0, saying it will be removed in Pillow 14 (2027-10-15) [P19] [P20] [P23] [P39].
Pixel density

The chapter says Pillow's PNG files are 72 pixels per inch by default, but a PNG saved with no dpi has no pHYs chunk and no density to read back, and with dpi=(72, 72) the chunk holds 2835 pixels per metre, which Pillow reads as 72.009 dpi; a JPEG saved with defaults has jfif_density (1, 1) and jfif_unit 0, no unit, and Matplotlib's PNG carries 100 dpi [P01] [P13] [P42]. The sums of the seating-card text are right, 4 by 5 inches at 72 pixels per inch is 288 by 360 pixels, and the ImageFont page says the size of truetype() is in pixels, not points [P01] [P11].
Project 16 as printed and as shipped

The four listings of Project 16 joined as printed stop with SyntaxError: invalid character U+2013 at line 38, because the listing writes width - logo_width with an en dash; with a minus sign, and as the shipped resizeAndAddLogo.py (SHA-256 starting 4291c7cedd9d), the program exits with 0 and turns zophie.png into 225 by 300 pixels, where 300 / 1088 * 816 is the float 225.00000000000003 [P01] [P02]. The test needs both sides above 300, so a 1200 by 250 strip and a 250 by 900 column keep their size while a 1200 by 400 panorama becomes 300 by 100 and a 500 by 700 picture 214 by 300, and C.PNG and e.JPG are skipped because the extension test is case sensitive [P01] [P47].
Table 21-1 and the colour names

Table 21-1 gives Green as (0, 255, 0, 255), but of its 8 rows only Green differs from Pillow 12.3.0, which returns (0, 128, 0, 255) for green and (0, 255, 0, 255) for lime, the two CSS values; ImageColor.colormap holds 148 names, from aliceblue to yellowgreen, where the Pillow page says some 140 and the chapter more than 100, and 'transparent' raises ValueError [P01] [P09] [P46].
The chapter replayed

The 138 statements of the chapter's 25 interactive listings (31 listings in all) were replayed as printed in four environments. With Python 3.14.6, Pillow 12.3.0 and Matplotlib 3.11.2, 131 of 138 matched the book headless and 135 on a virtual X display; with Pillow 10.4.0 and Matplotlib 3.9.2, the book's pins, built from source on 3.14.6, 125 matched headless and 108 on the display; with the same pins as wheels on Python 3.13.14, 129 and 108; with an empty Python, 15 [P01] [P05]. The 3 that still differ with the newest packages and a display are os.chdir to a Windows path (FileNotFoundError), the font arial.ttf (OSError) and the printed tuple of plt.pie, which is a PieContainer [P01] [P11] [P30].
The clipboard and the viewer

With xclip on a virtual X display pyperclipimg 0.2.0 copied a 40 by 30 RGB image and pasted it back as a PNG with equal pixels, and the clipboard offered image/png; with no DISPLAY copy() returned None and paste() raised ChildProcessError, with text on the clipboard paste() raised UnidentifiedImageError, and with no xclip the import raised NotImplementedError [P38] [P41] [P15]. Image.show() started xdg-open and the display program, and a screenshot of the screen matched 5 of 6 probe pixels of zophie.png [P16].
The fill of a rotation

The chapter says rotation gaps are black on Windows and transparent on macOS and Linux, but on Linux rotate(6) of the RGB zophie.png left (0, 0, 0) at the corner, an RGBA copy left (0, 0, 0, 0), and fillcolor='red' left (255, 0, 0): the fill follows the mode of the image, and the Pillow page of rotate() names a fill colour and no operating system; rotate(6, expand=True) of 816 by 1088 gives 926 by 1168 [P01] [P08].
The online materials

The online materials of the 3rd edition (7,759,877 bytes, 91 files, 72 of them Python) hold zophie.png (816 by 1088, mode RGB), catlogo.png (100 by 95, mode LA), guests.txt with 5 names and resizeAndAddLogo.py, and none of zophie_xmas_tree.png, me_and_zophie.png, zophie_the_cat.jpg or a file with flower in its name among 184 entries of the zip, although the chapter says a public domain flower image is also available [P01] [P02]. The book page of the publisher has 1 occurrence of Making Graphs and 0 of Pillow, Matplotlib, zophie or catlogo [P04].
The pins of Appendix A

Appendix A pins pillow==10.4.0 and matplotlib==3.92, and PyPI has no Matplotlib 3.92 among 85 plain-numbered releases, so uv answers that no version exists; the first CPython 3.14 wheel is Pillow 11.3.0 and Matplotlib 3.10.5, so the pins need a source build on Python 3.14 [P05] [P39] [P40]. Matplotlib 3.9.2 built from source on 3.14.6 but savefig() and legend() raised RecursionError, and its TkAgg backend failed with ImportError (Failed to load Tcl_SetVar) against Tk 9.0 in both Python 3.14.6 and Python 3.13.14, while Matplotlib 3.11.2 opened its windows [P37] [P50] [P51].
The second edition

The 2nd edition's chapter 19, Manipulating Images, mentions Pillow 30 times, textsize 3 times and ImageFont 13 times, and neither matplotlib nor pyperclipimg; the 3rd edition's chapter 21 adds Matplotlib, the clipboard and 3 practice programs, and uses neither textsize nor getsize [P01] [P07].
What pie and the colour cycle return

plt.pie() returned a tuple of 3 in Matplotlib 3.7.5 to 3.10.8 and returns a PieContainer in 3.11.0 and 3.11.2, which unpacks into 3 parts with autopct and 2 without it and whose len() raises TypeError; the Matplotlib page marks the change as in 3.11, and the first line colour #1f77b4 is stored as a text up to 3.10.8 and as a tuple of floats from 3.11.0 [P30] [P36] [P40]. The book's printed tuple matches its pinned Matplotlib and not the newest [P01].
plt.show and the figure

With the Agg backend, which Matplotlib chooses when there is no display, plt.show() returns None at once and the figure stays, so the axes held 2 lines and 0 collections, then 2 and 2, then 4 bars and then 8 patches at the four calls of savefig(); with a real Tk window plt.show() blocks, the figure list is then empty, a second show returns at once, and a savefig() after it writes a blank image of 1 colour, as the Matplotlib page says [P01] [P31] [P34]. Appendix B answer 12, that plt.show() cannot be called twice because it resets the graph data, is true for a window and not for Agg [P06].
title: Making graphs and manipulating images for an advanced course: chapter 21 and today's Pillow, ImageDraw, pyperclipimg and Matplotlib

nodes.label: Image fundamentals
nodes.body: The first part of the chapter, Computer Image Fundamentals, teaches the two ideas every Pillow call rests on: a colour is an RGBA value of four integers from 0 to 255, and a pixel is addressed by an x and y coordinate from the top-left origin, with box tuples naming rectangles (Sweigart, 2025). It then loads zophie.png as an Image object with size, format and save (Sweigart, 2025).

paras.text: The first part of the chapter, Computer Image Fundamentals, teaches the two ideas every Pillow call rests on: a colour is an RGBA value of four integers from 0 to 255, and a pixel is addressed by an x and y coordinate from the top-left origin, with box tuples naming rectangles (Sweigart, 2025). It then loads zophie.png as an Image object with size, format and save (Sweigart, 2025).

Three ideas carry this subject: colour representation covers the tuple, the names and the modes; the coordinate system covers the origin, the box tuple and its half-open edges; the image object covers opening, the filename, new images and saving. All of it was run with Pillow 12.3.0 on Python 3.14.6 and against the Pillow 10.4.0 the book pins, on the files of the publisher's zip, which the programs fetched and hash-checked (This study, 2026).

nodes.label: Color representation
nodes.body: The chapter explains an RGBA value as red, green, blue and alpha from 0 to 255, gives Table 21-1 of eight colour names, and says Pillow uses the same standard names as HTML and holds more than 100 of them in ImageColor.colormap (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow ImageColor page says the module converts CSS3-style colour specifiers and provides some 140 standard names, case insensitive, and the CSS Color module lists lime and green as separate colours (Pillow Developers, 2026)(World Wide Web Consortium, 2026).

Run against Pillow 12.3.0, the dictionary held 148 names, one value of Table 21-1 was wrong, and the two files of the chapter turned out to have different modes, RGB and LA, which matters as soon as a picture is saved or pasted (This study, 2026).

nodes.label: Rgba tuple
nodes.body: The chapter says Pillow writes red as (255, 0, 0, 255), that alpha 0 means invisible and that the other three numbers then do not matter (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow concepts page says an image has one or more bands, a PNG for example R, G, B and A, and that the mode is a string that defines the type and depth of a pixel (Pillow Developers, 2026).

The Pillow concepts page says an image has one or more bands, a PNG for example R, G, B and A, and that the mode is a string that defines the type and depth of a pixel (Pillow Developers, 2026).

Pillow 12.3.0 returned (255, 0, 0, 255) for red in RGBA and (255, 0, 0) in RGB; a new RGBA image started as (0, 0, 0, 0), and a pixel set to (10, 20, 30, 0) kept the numbers 10, 20 and 30 although it cannot be seen (This study, 2026). A program that tests for transparency must test the fourth number, not the colour.

nodes.definition: An RGBA value is a tuple of four integers from 0 to 255, red, green, blue and alpha; Pillow returns (255, 0, 0, 255) for red and (255, 0, 0) in mode RGB, a new RGBA image is filled with the invisible (0, 0, 0, 0), and a pixel with alpha 0 keeps its colour numbers but cannot be seen.

nodes.label: Coordinate system
nodes.body: The chapter teaches the pixel origin at the top-left corner with y growing downward, which it calls the opposite of school mathematics, and the box tuple of left, top, right and bottom with Figure 21-1 and Figure 21-2 (Sweigart, 2025). Pillow's tutorial uses the same box for crop() and paste() (Pillow Developers, 2026).

Pillow's tutorial uses the same box for crop() and paste() (Pillow Developers, 2026).

Three leaves cover it: where the origin is and what a pixel read outside the image does, what a box tuple holds, and why its right and bottom edges are left out. The sizes and the errors of this subject were produced by calling the methods, not by reading the text (This study, 2026).

nodes.label: Pixel origin
nodes.body: The chapter says (0, 0) is the top-left pixel, that x grows to the right, that y grows downward and that this bears repeating because it differs from mathematics (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow reference gives getpixel() the coordinate as (x, y) (Pillow Developers, 2026).

paras.text: The chapter says (0, 0) is the top-left pixel, that x grows to the right, that y grows downward and that this bears repeating because it differs from mathematics (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow reference gives getpixel() the coordinate as (x, y) (Pillow Developers, 2026).

On a 60 by 40 gradient the pixel (59, 0) was (236, 0, 177); getpixel((-1, 0)) returned the same colour, because a negative x counts from the right edge, while getpixel((60, 0)) and getpixel((0, 40)) raised IndexError with the text image index out of range (This study, 2026). The chapter does not mention that negative coordinates are accepted, which can hide an off-by-one error.

nodes.definition: A pixel is addressed by (x, y) with the origin (0, 0) at the top left, x growing to the right and y growing downward; the last pixel of a 60 by 40 image is (59, 39), (60, 0) raises IndexError with the text image index out of range, and a negative x such as -1 counts from the right edge and returns the pixel of x 59.

nodes.label: Box tuple
nodes.body: The chapter defines the box as left, top, right and bottom, says right and bottom are one pixel beyond the edge, and shows (3, 1, 9, 6) in Figure 21-2 (Sweigart, 2025). Appendix B answer 3 says the four integers are left, top, width and height, which contradicts it (Sweigart, 2025).

paras.text: The chapter defines the box as left, top, right and bottom, says right and bottom are one pixel beyond the edge, and shows (3, 1, 9, 6) in Figure 21-2 (Sweigart, 2025). Appendix B answer 3 says the four integers are left, top, width and height, which contradicts it (Sweigart, 2025).

The box (3, 1, 9, 6) cropped from a 28 by 27 image gave the size (6, 5), a width of 9 minus 3 and a height of 6 minus 1, which is 30 pixels, so the chapter's definition is right and the answer of Appendix B is wrong (This study, 2026). A program that passes width and height as the third and fourth numbers crops a different region without any error.

nodes.body: The chapter notes that a box includes the left column and top row but not the right column and bottom row (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow reference calls the crop box a 4-tuple of the left, upper, right and lower pixel coordinate (Pillow Developers, 2026).

crop((10, 5, 40, 35)) of the 60 by 40 gradient gave 30 by 30; crop((50, 30, 70, 50)) gave 20 by 20 whose last pixel was black (0, 0, 0); a box with right 10 less than left 40 raised ValueError with the text Coordinate 'right' is less than 'left', and a box with right equal to left gave the size (0, 30) without an error (This study, 2026). nodes.definition: A box includes its left and top edge and excludes its right and bottom edge, so crop((10, 5, 40, 35)) of a 60 by 40 image is 30 by 30; a box past the edge still gives the full size 20 by 20 with black pixels outside, a box with right less than left raises ValueError, and a box with right equal to left gives width 0.

nodes.label: New image
nodes.body: The chapter makes a 100 by 200 purple image, calls Image.new() again with no colour for a 20 by 20 image and says the default is the invisible black (0, 0, 0, 0) (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow reference says the colour default of Image.new() is black and that colour strings are accepted for RGB images (Pillow Developers, 2026).

paras.text: The chapter makes a 100 by 200 purple image, calls Image.new() again with no colour for a 20 by 20 image and says the default is the invisible black (0, 0, 0, 0) (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow reference says the colour default of Image.new() is black and that colour strings are accepted for RGB images (Pillow Developers, 2026).

The purple image had the pixel (128, 0, 128, 255), the colourless RGBA image (0, 0, 0, 0) and a colourless RGB image (0, 0, 0), which is opaque black; the colour from ImageColor.getcolor('purple', 'RGBA') gave the same pixel as the name (This study, 2026). The chapter's remark about invisible black holds for RGBA only.

nodes.definition: Image.new(mode, size, color) makes a blank image: with no colour an RGBA image is the invisible (0, 0, 0, 0) and an RGB image is black (0, 0, 0), and the colour may be a name such as 'purple', which gives (128, 0, 128, 255) for the 100 by 200 image of the chapter, or a tuple from ImageColor.getcolor().

nodes.label: Save formats
nodes.body: The chapter saves zophie.png as zophie.jpg and says Pillow sees the extension .jpg and uses the JPEG format, and that the two files are not identical (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow reference says save() takes the format from the file name extension when none is given, the format page gives the JPEG option quality a default of 75, and the PNG specification defines the pHYs chunk for pixel density (Pillow Developers, 2026)(World Wide Web Consortium, 2026).

paras.text: The chapter saves zophie.png as zophie.jpg and says Pillow sees the extension .jpg and uses the JPEG format, and that the two files are not identical (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow reference says save() takes the format from the file name extension when none is given, the format page gives the JPEG option quality a default of 75, and the PNG specification defines the pHYs chunk for pixel density (Pillow Developers, 2026)(World Wide Web Consortium, 2026).

The JPEG was 125,433 bytes against the 1,287,443 bytes of the PNG, and the largest difference in a channel after reading it back was 37, so the chapter's not identical means lossy; saving as .unknownext raised ValueError with the text unknown file extension (This study, 2026). The chapter does not say that the JPEG quality, 75 by default, trades size for loss.

nodes.label: Image editing
nodes.body: The second part of the chapter, Manipulating Images with Pillow, edits an opened picture with a handful of methods: crop(), copy(), paste(), resize(), rotate() and transpose(), and getpixel() and putpixel() for single pixels (Sweigart, 2025). The summary lists the same six methods and save() (Sweigart, 2025).

paras.text: The second part of the chapter, Manipulating Images with Pillow, edits an opened picture with a handful of methods: crop(), copy(), paste(), resize(), rotate() and transpose(), and getpixel() and putpixel() for single pixels (Sweigart, 2025). The summary lists the same six methods and save() (Sweigart, 2025).

Three ideas carry this subject: cropping and pasting cover the box, the in-place paste, the mask and the tile loop; resizing and rotating cover the integer size, the filter and the fill and expanded size; flipping and pixel access cover transpose and the two pixel calls. Every size and colour below was measured on the shipped zophie.png and on a 60 by 40 gradient made by the program (This study, 2026).

nodes.label: Crop and paste
nodes.body: The chapter crops the face out of zophie.png, copies the picture, pastes the face twice, and tiles it with two nested loops, noting that crop() returns a new image and paste() changes its own (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow reference describes both calls (Pillow Developers, 2026).

paras.text: The chapter crops the face out of zophie.png, copies the picture, pastes the face twice, and tiles it with two nested loops, noting that crop() returns a new image and paste() changes its own (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow reference describes both calls (Pillow Developers, 2026).

Four leaves cover it: the crop box, the in-place paste of a copy, the transparency mask and the tile loop. In Pillow 12.3.0 the crop gave 230 by 215, paste returned None, a missing mask copied a transparent pixel as (255, 255, 255, 0) and the loop made 24 pastes (This study, 2026).

nodes.label: Crop box
nodes.body: The chapter says crop() takes a box tuple, returns a new Image and leaves the original untouched, and crops the face with (335, 345, 565, 560) (Sweigart, 2025). Appendix B answer 6 gives im.crop((0, 50, 50, 50)) for a quarter of a picture (Sweigart, 2025).

paras.text: The chapter says crop() takes a box tuple, returns a new Image and leaves the original untouched, and crops the face with (335, 345, 565, 560) (Sweigart, 2025). Appendix B answer 6 gives im.crop((0, 50, 50, 50)) for a quarter of a picture (Sweigart, 2025).

The face was 230 by 215 pixels in mode RGB, the original stayed 816 by 1088, and the returned object was a different one (This study, 2026). The box of Appendix B answer 6 has the same top and bottom, so its height is 0; the quarter it names needs (0, 50, 50, 100).

nodes.label: Paste in place
nodes.body: The chapter says copy() returns a new Image so the original can be kept, that paste() modifies its Image in place and does not return one, and that copy() and paste() do not use the clipboard (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow reference gives the paste box as a 2-tuple for the upper left corner and says a pasted image of another mode is converted to the mode of the target (Pillow Developers, 2026).

paras.text: The chapter says copy() returns a new Image so the original can be kept, that paste() modifies its Image in place and does not return one, and that copy() and paste() do not use the clipboard (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow reference gives the paste box as a 2-tuple for the upper left corner and says a pasted image of another mode is converted to the mode of the target (Pillow Developers, 2026).

paste() returned None; after pasting the 230 by 215 face at (0, 0) into a copy the copy's corner pixel equalled the face's and differed from the original's, which was untouched, and the copy was a different object from the original (This study, 2026). A program that writes im = im.paste(...) loses its image, because the name then holds None.

nodes.label: Paste mask
nodes.body: The chapter says an image with transparency must be passed as the optional third argument, otherwise its transparent pixels appear as white pixels, and it shows both results in Figure 21-13 (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow reference says a mask of mode 1, L, LA, RGBA or RGBa updates only the regions it indicates, that the alpha band is used as the mask if present, and that where the mask is 0 the current value is kept (Pillow Developers, 2026).

paras.text: The chapter says an image with transparency must be passed as the optional third argument, otherwise its transparent pixels appear as white pixels, and it shows both results in Figure 21-13 (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow reference says a mask of mode 1, L, LA, RGBA or RGBa updates only the regions it indicates, that the alpha band is used as the mask if present, and that where the mask is 0 the current value is kept (Pillow Developers, 2026).

On a red RGBA background the corner of catlogo.png pasted with itself as the mask stayed (200, 0, 0, 255), and pasted without a mask became (255, 255, 255, 0); a pixel in the middle of the cat was the same in both (This study, 2026). The white of the book's figure exists because the stored colour under alpha 0 in this logo is 255, the L value of its first pixel (255, 0), so a logo saved with a black fill would give black.

nodes.label: Tile loop
nodes.body: The chapter tiles the 230 by 215 face over the 816 by 1088 picture with a loop over left in range(0, width, face width) and an inner loop over top, and prints the positions from (0, 0) to (690, 1075) (Sweigart, 2025). Nothing in the chapter says what happens at the right and bottom edge, where the last tiles do not fit.

paras.text: The chapter tiles the 230 by 215 face over the 816 by 1088 picture with a loop over left in range(0, width, face width) and an inner loop over top, and prints the positions from (0, 0) to (690, 1075) (Sweigart, 2025). Nothing in the chapter says what happens at the right and bottom edge, where the last tiles do not fit.

The loop made 4 columns and 6 rows, 24 pastes, the first three at (0, 0), (0, 215) and (0, 430) and the last two at (690, 860) and (690, 1075), the same positions the chapter prints; the last column and the last row run past the edge and are cut off without an error (This study, 2026). Counting the pastes first, 4 times 6, is the check the practice program asks for with 6 times 10.

nodes.label: Resize and rotate
nodes.body: The chapter resizes the cat to half its width and height and to a taller shape, and rotates it by 90, 180, 270 and 6 degrees, with and without expand (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow reference documents resize() with a resample argument and rotate() with expand and fillcolor (Pillow Developers, 2026).

paras.text: The chapter resizes the cat to half its width and height and to a taller shape, and rotates it by 90, 180, 270 and 6 degrees, with and without expand (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow reference documents resize() with a resample argument and rotate() with expand and fillcolor (Pillow Developers, 2026).

Four leaves cover it: the integer size, the filter nobody names, the fill of the corners and the expanded size. Pillow 12.3.0 refused a float size, used bicubic by default, filled an RGB corner with black and made 6 degrees of rotation 926 by 1168 (This study, 2026).

nodes.label: Resize integer
nodes.body: The chapter says resize() accepts only integers in its tuple, which is why both divisions are wrapped in int(), and that it returns a new Image (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow reference gives size as the requested size in pixels, (width, height) (Pillow Developers, 2026).

paras.text: The chapter says resize() accepts only integers in its tuple, which is why both divisions are wrapped in int(), and that it returns a new Image (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow reference gives size as the requested size in pixels, (width, height) (Pillow Developers, 2026).

int(width / 2) and int(height / 2) gave 408 by 544 from 816 by 1088; the taller shape gave 816 by 1388; and a size of w / 2, h / 2, the floats 408.0 and 544.0, raised TypeError with the text 'float' object cannot be interpreted as an integer, while the original stayed 816 by 1088 (This study, 2026). Integer division with // would do the same without the int() call.

nodes.label: Resize filter
nodes.body: The chapter does not name a resampling filter and calls resize() with a size only (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow reference says the default filter is Resampling.BICUBIC, except for modes 1 and P, which always use NEAREST, and lists NEAREST, BOX, BILINEAR, HAMMING, BICUBIC and LANCZOS (Pillow Developers, 2026).

paras.text: The chapter does not name a resampling filter and calls resize() with a size only (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow reference says the default filter is Resampling.BICUBIC, except for modes 1 and P, which always use NEAREST, and lists NEAREST, BOX, BILINEAR, HAMMING, BICUBIC and LANCZOS (Pillow Developers, 2026).

On the 60 by 40 gradient resized to 30 by 20 the bytes of the default call equalled those of Image.Resampling.BICUBIC and differed from NEAREST and from LANCZOS (This study, 2026). The choice of a filter changes the pixels of every scaled picture of Project 16, and the chapter leaves it at the default.

nodes.definition: When no resample filter is given resize() uses bicubic for an RGB image, so its bytes equal those of Image.Resampling.BICUBIC and differ from NEAREST and from LANCZOS; the book never names a filter, and the argument resample= is the way to choose one.

nodes.label: Rotate fill
nodes.body: The chapter says rotated images keep their size, that on Windows a black background fills the gaps and that on macOS and Linux transparent pixels fill them instead (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow reference describes fillcolor of rotate() as an optional colour for the area outside the rotated image and names no operating system (Pillow Developers, 2026).

paras.text: The chapter says rotated images keep their size, that on Windows a black background fills the gaps and that on macOS and Linux transparent pixels fill them instead (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow reference describes fillcolor of rotate() as an optional colour for the area outside the rotated image and names no operating system (Pillow Developers, 2026).

On the RGB gradient the corner after rotate(6) was (0, 0, 0), on an RGBA copy it was (0, 0, 0, 0) and with fillcolor='red' it was (255, 0, 0); the size stayed 60 by 40 in both rotations (This study, 2026). The result follows the image's mode, not the operating system,.

nodes.definition: rotate() turns an image counterclockwise and keeps its size, and the corners that no pixel reaches are filled with black (0, 0, 0) in mode RGB and with the invisible (0, 0, 0, 0) in mode RGBA; the keyword fillcolor, for example 'red', replaces the fill, so the colour depends on the image's mode.

nodes.label: Rotate expand
nodes.body: The chapter says expand=True enlarges the image to fit the whole rotated picture and that with 90, 180 or 270 degrees the result has no black or transparent background (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow reference describes expand as making the output image large enough to hold the entire rotated image (Pillow Developers, 2026).

paras.text: The chapter says expand=True enlarges the image to fit the whole rotated picture and that with 90, 180 or 270 degrees the result has no black or transparent background (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow reference describes expand as making the output image large enough to hold the entire rotated image (Pillow Developers, 2026).

Without expand rotate(90), rotate(180) and rotate(6) all gave 816 by 1088; with expand=True rotate(90) gave 1088 by 816, rotate(180) gave 816 by 1088 and rotate(6) gave 926 by 1168 (This study, 2026). The tiling loop of the same picture would need 926 by 1168 to be recomputed, which is why a program should read the size again after an expanded rotation.

nodes.label: Flip and pixels
nodes.body: The chapter mirrors the picture with transpose() and the constants Image.FLIP_LEFT_RIGHT and Image.FLIP_TOP_BOTTOM, and reads and sets single pixels with getpixel() and putpixel(), colouring half a 100 by 100 image grey (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow release notes of 9.1.0 moved the constants to Image.Transpose and those of 9.4.0 restored the old names (Pillow Developers, 2026).

paras.text: The chapter mirrors the picture with transpose() and the constants Image.FLIP_LEFT_RIGHT and Image.FLIP_TOP_BOTTOM, and reads and sets single pixels with getpixel() and putpixel(), colouring half a 100 by 100 image grey (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow release notes of 9.1.0 moved the constants to Image.Transpose and those of 9.4.0 restored the old names (Pillow Developers, 2026).

Two leaves cover it: flipping and the pixel calls. In Pillow 12.3.0 the old constant was the integer 0, equal to Image.Transpose.FLIP_LEFT_RIGHT, so the chapter's code runs, and putpixel() with an RGB tuple on an RGBA image stored alpha 255 (This study, 2026).

nodes.label: Logo project
nodes.body: Project 16, Add a Logo, is the chapter's one complete program: it resizes every .png and .jpg file of the working directory to fit a 300 by 300 square, pastes catlogo.png into the bottom-right corner and saves the result in a folder named withLogo, in four steps that open the logo, loop over the files, resize and paste (Sweigart, 2025).

The program was run as the page prints it, which fails, and as the publisher's file ships it, which runs, and its edge cases were measured with pictures made by the program (This study, 2026).

paras.text: The chapter writes Hello with no font argument and says the typeface and size are not customised (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow release notes of 10.1.0 say a version of Aileron Regular that can be drawn at chosen sizes is now loaded, and the reference says load_default() takes a size (Pillow Developers, 2026).

load_default() returned a FreeTypeFont of size 10 named Aileron Regular, and load_default(size=20) one of size 20; across the 14 Pillow releases run the class was ImageFont in 9.5.0 and 10.0.0 and FreeTypeFont from 10.1.0, and size= raised TypeError before 10.1.0 (This study, 2026). Hello drawn with no font argument therefore differs between Pillow 10.0.0 and 10.1.0, and the pinned 10.4.0 draws the sized FreeType font.

nodes.label: Clipboard and viewer
nodes.body: The chapter's show() opens the picture in a window for debugging, and the section on the clipboard says pyperclipimg.copy() puts a Pillow Image on the operating system's clipboard and paste() returns the clipboard's image (Sweigart, 2025). The pyperclipimg README names xclip or wl-copy as the programs it needs on Linux (Sweigart, 2024).

paras.text: The chapter's show() opens the picture in a window for debugging, and the section on the clipboard says pyperclipimg.copy() puts a Pillow Image on the operating system's clipboard and paste() returns the clipboard's image (Sweigart, 2025). The pyperclipimg README names xclip or wl-copy as the programs it needs on Linux (Sweigart, 2024).

Three leaves cover it: the viewer that show() starts, the round trip through the clipboard and the ways the clipboard fails. The programs ran on a virtual X display with xclip and the display program of ImageMagick, and a screenshot of that screen found the picture (This study, 2026).

nodes.label: Show viewer
nodes.body: The chapter says show() opens the image in a window and is useful when debugging (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow ImageShow page lists XDGViewer, which runs the freedesktop.org xdg-open command, and DisplayViewer, the ImageMagick display command, among the Unix viewers registered if their command is found, and says the temporary files created from images are not removed (Pillow Developers, 2026).

paras.text: The chapter says show() opens the image in a window and is useful when debugging (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow ImageShow page lists XDGViewer, which runs the freedesktop.org xdg-open command, and DisplayViewer, the ImageMagick display command, among the Unix viewers registered if their command is found, and says the temporary files created from images are not removed (Pillow Developers, 2026).

On the virtual display Image.show() returned None and started xdg-open and the display program, and a screenshot of the screen matched 5 of 6 probe pixels of zophie.png at one position; Pillow listed XDGViewer and DisplayViewer first, and with no viewer on the PATH the headless replay showed nothing and raised no error (This study, 2026). A program therefore cannot learn from show() whether anything was shown.

nodes.body: The chapter shows only the working case and tells the reader to copy a new image from a graphics program before paste() (Sweigart, 2025). The README says the module needs xclip or wl-copy on Linux (Sweigart, 2024).

nodes.label: Matplotlib graphs
nodes.body: The last part of the chapter makes graphs with Matplotlib: a line graph and a scatter plot of the same two series, a bar graph and a pie chart, and then markers, colours, labels and a legend, saving with plt.savefig() and previewing with plt.show() (Sweigart, 2025). The Matplotlib interface guide calls pyplot an implicit interface that keeps track of the last Figure and Axes created (Matplotlib Development Team, 2026).

paras.text: The last part of the chapter makes graphs with Matplotlib: a line graph and a scatter plot of the same two series, a bar graph and a pie chart, and then markers, colours, labels and a legend, saving with plt.savefig() and previewing with plt.show() (Sweigart, 2025). The Matplotlib interface guide calls pyplot an implicit interface that keeps track of the last Figure and Axes created (Matplotlib Development Team, 2026).

Four ideas carry this subject: the figure model covers the current figure, its defaults and the backend; line and scatter cover the two plot calls; bar and pie cover the other two charts; decorations and output cover labels, saving and the show lifecycle. Everything ran under Matplotlib 3.11.2 and, for the book's pin, 3.9.2, with the Agg backend and with a real Tk window on a virtual display (This study, 2026).

nodes.label: Figure model
nodes.body: The chapter calls plt a short name for matplotlib.pyplot, says a figure is the window that holds one or more plots and that Matplotlib picks colours and size by itself (Sweigart, 2025). The Matplotlib guide to its interfaces says pyplot keeps a list of figures and that gcf and gca return the current figure and axes (Matplotlib Development Team, 2026).

paras.text: The chapter calls plt a short name for matplotlib.pyplot, says a figure is the window that holds one or more plots and that Matplotlib picks colours and size by itself (Sweigart, 2025). The Matplotlib guide to its interfaces says pyplot keeps a list of figures and that gcf and gca return the current figure and axes (Matplotlib Development Team, 2026).

Three leaves cover it: how state piles up in the current figure, the defaults of a figure, and the backend choice. A figure was 640 by 480 pixels, a second plot call added a second line to the same axes, and the backend was agg with no display and tkagg with one (This study, 2026).

nodes.label: Pyplot state
nodes.body: The chapter calls plt.plot() twice to put two lines on one graph, saves with savefig() and calls plt.show() (Sweigart, 2025). The Matplotlib interface guide calls pyplot an implicit interface that keeps track of the last Figure and Axes created and adds artists to the object it thinks the user wants (Matplotlib Development Team, 2026).

paras.text: The chapter calls plt.plot() twice to put two lines on one graph, saves with savefig() and calls plt.show() (Sweigart, 2025). The Matplotlib interface guide calls pyplot an implicit interface that keeps track of the last Figure and Axes created and adds artists to the object it thinks the user wants (Matplotlib Development Team, 2026).

With Agg two plot() calls made 2 lines, plt.show() returned None at once and figure 1 stayed open, and a following plt.scatter() added 1 collection to the same axes (This study, 2026). In the headless replay each later example drew on the figure of the earlier ones: at the four calls of savefig() the axes held 2 lines and 0 collections, 2 lines and 2 collections, 2 lines and 2 collections with 4 bars, and the same with 8 patches for the pie, whereas with a window each plt.show() emptied them and the pie figure held only its 4 wedges.

nodes.definition: pyplot keeps one current figure and axes, and every plot call draws on them: two plot() calls give 2 lines, plt.show() with the Agg backend returns None and leaves the figure, and a following plt.scatter() adds 1 collection to the same axes, so state piles up from one example to the next.

nodes.label: Figure defaults
nodes.body: The chapter says Matplotlib selects colours for the lines and an appropriate size for the graph automatically, and does not give the size (Sweigart, 2025). The Matplotlib savefig reference documents the dpi argument (Matplotlib Development Team, 2026).

paras.text: The chapter says Matplotlib selects colours for the lines and an appropriate size for the graph automatically, and does not give the size (Sweigart, 2025). The Matplotlib savefig reference documents the dpi argument (Matplotlib Development Team, 2026).

A new figure was 6.4 by 4.8 inches at 100 dpi, which is 640 by 480 pixels, and the first line colour was #1f77b4 in every release; but the colour cycle held texts such as '#1f77b4' in 3.7.5 to 3.10.8 and tuples of floats in 3.11.0 and 3.11.2 (This study, 2026). The chapter prints neither, so only the size of the saved PNGs can be compared with the figures of the book.

nodes.body: The chapter says plt.show() opens a window with the graph and that the window is interactive, and says nothing about a program that has no window (Sweigart, 2025). The Matplotlib backends guide separates interactive backends such as TkAgg from non-interactive ones such as Agg (Matplotlib Development Team, 2026).

paras.text: The chapter says plt.show() opens a window with the graph and that the window is interactive, and says nothing about a program that has no window (Sweigart, 2025). The Matplotlib backends guide separates interactive backends such as TkAgg from non-interactive ones such as Agg (Matplotlib Development Team, 2026).

With no DISPLAY Matplotlib 3.11.2 chose agg and with a display it chose tkagg, and matplotlib.is_interactive() was False (This study, 2026). The first choice is why the chapter's listings run to the end in a container without opening a window.

nodes.label: Line and scatter
nodes.body: The chapter says a line graph is ideal for showing changes in one measure over time and makes it with plt.plot() twice, then makes the scatter plot of the same data with plt.scatter(), noting that the code is identical except for the function name (Sweigart, 2025). The Matplotlib pages document both functions (Matplotlib Development Team, 2026).

The Matplotlib pages document both functions (Matplotlib Development Team, 2026).

Two leaves cover it: the line plot and the scatter plot. plot() returned a list holding one Line2D, scatter() a PathCollection stored beside the lines and not among them, and the two series got the colours #1f77b4 and #ff7f0e (This study, 2026).

nodes.body: The chapter plots x_values against y_values1 and y_values2 and shows the shell returning a list for each call, and the first values of the two lists belong together (Sweigart, 2025). The Matplotlib reference says plot() returns a list of Line2D objects (Matplotlib Development Team, 2026).

plot() returned a list of 1 Line2D whose y data were 10, 13, 15, 18, 16 and 20, and the colours of the two lines were #1f77b4 and #ff7f0e (This study, 2026). In Matplotlib 3.11 the colour is kept as a tuple of floats and not as a text.

nodes.label: Bar and pie
nodes.body: The chapter says a bar graph compares the same data in different categories, that unlike a line graph the order of categories is not important, and that a pie chart has labels and slices and an autopct format string (Sweigart, 2025). The Matplotlib pages for bar() and pie() document both (Matplotlib Development Team, 2026).

paras.text: The chapter says a bar graph compares the same data in different categories, that unlike a line graph the order of categories is not important, and that a pie chart has labels and slices and an autopct format string (Sweigart, 2025). The Matplotlib pages for bar() and pie() document both (Matplotlib Development Team, 2026).

Two leaves cover it: the bar chart and the pie chart. bar() returned a BarContainer in the order given, and pie() returned a tuple in Matplotlib 3.10 and earlier and a PieContainer in 3.11, which the 3.11 API changes name (This study, 2026).

nodes.label: Bar chart
nodes.body: The chapter calls plt.bar(categories, values) with the four categories Cats, Dogs, Mice and Moose and the values 100 to 400 and says the order of categories is not important (Sweigart, 2025). The Matplotlib reference says bar() returns a BarContainer and accepts categorical x values (Matplotlib Development Team, 2026).

paras.text: The chapter calls plt.bar(categories, values) with the four categories Cats, Dogs, Mice and Moose and the values 100 to 400 and says the order of categories is not important (Sweigart, 2025). The Matplotlib reference says bar() returns a BarContainer and accepts categorical x values (Matplotlib Development Team, 2026).

bar() returned a BarContainer, the heights were 100, 200, 300 and 400 as numpy int64 values and the tick labels were the four names in the given order, so the chart is not sorted (This study, 2026). The values come back as numpy integers, not Python ints, which matters when they are printed or compared with JSON.

nodes.label: Pie chart

nodes.label: Show lifecycle
nodes.body: The chapter says plt.show() blocks until the window is closed, that closing it resets the graph data so a second plt.show() does nothing or shows an empty window, and that plt.savefig() must come first (Sweigart, 2025). Appendix B answer 12 says you cannot call plt.show() twice in a row because it resets the graph data (Sweigart, 2025). The Matplotlib show reference says that at the end of a blocking show() the figure is closed and unregistered from pyplot and that calling savefig() afterwards would save a new and thus empty figure (Matplotlib Development Team, 2026).

Appendix B answer 12 says you cannot call plt.show() twice in a row because it resets the graph data (Sweigart, 2025). The Matplotlib show reference says that at the end of a blocking show() the figure is closed and unregistered from pyplot and that calling savefig() afterwards would save a new and thus empty figure (Matplotlib Development Team, 2026).

With Agg plt.show() returned None at once, the figure stayed and a savefig() after it still held the line; with a real Tk window it blocked until the window closed, the figure list was then empty, a second show returned at once, and a savefig() after the window saved a blank image of 1 colour, while showing a new empty figure blocked again (This study, 2026). The chapter's rule holds for a window and the answer of Appendix B holds for it only.

Four ideas carry this subject: install and versions cover the pins and the Python they run on; book corrections cover the statements and files that do not hold; deprecated interfaces cover what the newest Pillow removed or warns about; the practice programs were written from the chapter's text and run. The sources that the chapter itself points to were fetched on the day, and the zip of the publisher was fetched and hash-checked at run time (This study, 2026). The chapter page returned 200 with 119,144 bytes, holds 31 listings, 20 figures and 1 table, and its sha256 equals the chapterDigest of the book's own chapter ontology; nothing ran on Windows or macOS, the PDFs of the JPEG standard and of JFIF were reached but not searched, the commit the course pins was not opened, and the photograph of the stories was not fetched because the single request to Wikimedia Commons answered 429 (This study, 2026).

nodes.body: The chapter tells the reader to install Pillow, Matplotlib and pyperclipimg by Appendix A, which pins pillow==10.4.0 and matplotlib==3.92 and lists pyperclipimg with no number (Sweigart, 2025). PyPI lists the releases and the Python each one supports (Python Package Index, 2026).

Four leaves cover it: the pins, the first wheels for Python 3.14, the pinned Matplotlib built from source and the Tk 9.0 clash. On Python 3.14.6 the pinned Pillow built and ran, the pinned Matplotlib built but could not draw, and its window backend could not load (This study, 2026). The 138 statements of the chapter's 25 interactive listings, replayed as printed, matched 131 headless and 135 on a virtual X display with the newest packages, 125 and 108 with the pins built on 3.14.6, 129 and 108 with the pins as wheels on Python 3.13.14, and 15 with an empty Python.

PyPI listed no CPython 3.14 wheel for Pillow before 11.3.0 and none for Matplotlib before 3.10.5, so the pinned Pillow 10.4.0 and Matplotlib 3.9.2, which have 3.13 wheels, need a compiler and the libjpeg, FreeType and Qhull headers under 3.14 (This study, 2026). Five leaves cover them: the green of Table 21-1, the 72 pixels per inch, the rotation fill, the answers of Appendix B and the missing files. Each was found by running the statement, not by comparing texts, and each has a number or a name in its leaf (This study, 2026).

nodes.label: Green table error
nodes.body: Table 21-1 lists eight names and says they are standard HTML colour names, among them Green as (0, 255, 0, 255) and Gray as (128, 128, 128, 255) (Sweigart, 2025). The CSS Color module lists green as #008000, which is 0 128 0, and lime as #00ff00, which is 0 255 0 (World Wide Web Consortium, 2026).

paras.text: Table 21-1 lists eight names and says they are standard HTML colour names, among them Green as (0, 255, 0, 255) and Gray as (128, 128, 128, 255) (Sweigart, 2025). The CSS Color module lists green as #008000, which is 0 128 0, and lime as #00ff00, which is 0 255 0 (World Wide Web Consortium, 2026).

Of the 8 rows only one differed: ImageColor.getcolor('Green', 'RGBA') was (0, 128, 0, 255) and 'Lime' was (0, 255, 0, 255), so the printed value belongs to lime (This study, 2026). The value Pillow returns is the CSS one.

nodes.definition: Table 21-1 gives Green as (0, 255, 0, 255), but checking all 8 rows of the table against ImageColor.getcolor() finds one that differs: 'Green' is (0, 128, 0, 255) and the table's value belongs to 'Lime', the HTML name of full green.

nodes.label: Dpi claim
nodes.body: The chapter says Pillow creates PNG images that are 72 pixels per inch by default and that a 4 by 5 inch card would require 288 by 360 pixels (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow format page documents the dpi option of the PNG writer and the PNG specification defines the pHYs chunk (Pillow Developers, 2026)(World Wide Web Consortium, 2026).

paras.text: The chapter says Pillow creates PNG images that are 72 pixels per inch by default and that a 4 by 5 inch card would require 288 by 360 pixels (Sweigart, 2025). The Pillow format page documents the dpi option of the PNG writer and the PNG specification defines the pHYs chunk (Pillow Developers, 2026)(World Wide Web Consortium, 2026).

A PNG saved with no dpi had no pHYs chunk and no dpi to read back; with dpi=(72, 72) the chunk held 2835 pixels per metre and Pillow read it back as 72.009, and the sums 288 / 72 and 360 / 72 gave 4 and 5 inches (This study, 2026). A JPEG saved with defaults had a jfif_density of (1, 1) with unit 0, which is no unit.

nodes.definition: The chapter says Pillow's PNG files are 72 pixels per inch by default, but a PNG saved with no dpi has no pHYs chunk at all and no density to read back; with dpi=(72, 72) the chunk holds 2835 pixels per metre, which reads back as 72.009 dots per inch, so the 288 by 360 card needs the argument.

Two leaves cover it: textsize and getsize, which are gone, and getdata, which warns. Across the 14 Pillow releases run, textsize and getsize existed only in 9.5.0, and the warning for getdata appeared in 12.1.0, 12.2.0 and 12.3.0 (This study, 2026).

nodes.label: Textsize gone
nodes.body: The 2nd edition's chapter 19 mentions Pillow 30 times, ImageFont 13 times and textsize 3 times, and neither matplotlib nor pyperclipimg, and the Pillow release notes of 10.0.0 say ImageDraw.textsize() and ImageFont.getsize() were removed in favour of textbbox(), textlength() and getbbox() (Sweigart, 2019)(Pillow Developers, 2026). The 3rd edition's chapter does not use them (Sweigart, 2025).

paras.text: The 2nd edition's chapter 19 mentions Pillow 30 times, ImageFont 13 times and textsize 3 times, and neither matplotlib nor pyperclipimg, and the Pillow release notes of 10.0.0 say ImageDraw.textsize() and ImageFont.getsize() were removed in favour of textbbox(), textlength() and getbbox() (Sweigart, 2019)(Pillow Developers, 2026). The 3rd edition's chapter does not use them (Sweigart, 2025).

In 12.3.0 hasattr gave False for ImageDraw.textsize and for FreeTypeFont.getsize and True for textbbox, textlength and getbbox; the 14 releases split at 9.5.0, which had both, and 10.0.0, which had neither (This study, 2026).
